children: Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) shares surged more than 8 percent on Monday, recording their biggest intraday gain in over six years, after the company reported record earnings for the September quarter and received bullish brokerage commentary. The stock emerged as the top gainer on the Nifty and the biggest contributor to the benchmark index's gains.

The rally pushed Reliance Industries' market capitalisation past Rs 17 lakh crore, with the stock climbing to an intraday high of Rs 1,259, up 8.1 percent. The shares recorded their biggest single-day intraday gain since April 2020 and were the most actively traded on both the NSE and BSE.

Market expert Rakesh Bansal told CNBC-AWAAZ that Reliance shares are showing signs of a strong technical breakout and could see further gains. According to Bansal, the stock has crossed the crucial Rs 1,234 level and was trading around Rs 1,252-1,253.
Reliance shares: Key levels to watch
Bansal sees Rs 1,325 as the next important target for the stock from a trading perspective. He said the company's record profit and strong quarterly performance have provided support to the shares.
From a longer-term perspective, he sees the stock potentially moving towards Rs 1,500, an upside of 33 percent from its closing levels of the previous session.
The company's Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C) business reported a 68 percent increase in EBITDA in the September quarter, adding to investor confidence, he said.
The performance of Reliance's other businesses and the potential for value unlocking have also remained important factors in the investment outlook.
Bansal also highlighted the potential value of Reliance's stake in Jio Platforms, whose market valuation is estimated at around Rs 13 lakh crore.
He said Reliance's holding in Jio Platforms could provide further scope for value creation for the parent company.
Potential stake sales or partial stake dilution in Reliance Retail could also lead to value unlocking, according to the market expert.
Reliance has previously unlocked value through the listing of Jio Financial Services, and similar initiatives involving its other businesses could provide further opportunities.

Virat Jagad, Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza, added, "Reliance Industries is showing a strong recovery with a sharp bullish candle backed by significant volume, indicating fresh buying interest. The stock is attempting to break above its descending channel resistance near Rs 1,255 and has moved above the 20 and 50 EMAs. RSI has improved above 60, supporting positive momentum. A sustained breakout could open the way towards Rs 1,346, while Rs 1,250 remains a crucial support."

Reliance Industries reported its strongest-ever quarterly financial performance for the July-September quarter, with record revenue, EBITDA and net profit, supported by robust growth in its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, digital services and retail operations.
